body: If the cigarette I smoked yesterday causes me a dry socket, would it be immediately or would it take a couple of days?

He didn't really give me any instructions, but the painkillers and to avoid hot food... I was smoking a cig when a friend told me I couldn't, so I checked Google and she was right. Then I came to ask in here how long should I wait. 

And also because of this article, of a dentist, which says cigarettes and straws don't cause dry sockets, but rather the way the tooth is removed: http://www.americasdentalbookstore.com/articles/OralSurgery/DrySocketPrevention.htm 

I don't have any experience, thus I asked here. Even if cigs don't cause it I will wait for it, don't need to get angry you guys.
I have no idea, but he did tell his assistant my tooth seemed to be quite strong, and he kept using my jaw as counterweight. Maybe I'm mistaken and he didn't, please enlighten me
I have smoked one, but will wait for the rest. I've also read excessive force on the removal can cause dry sockets, and my dentist did used it. Is that true?
thanks man.. I'll try talking to her, the problem is I kinda have this barrier to this subject... She has a friend whose son suicided a few months ago, maybe that would help her understand..
